references.text: The same expression 'the Lord, the God of the Hebrews' is used when Moses is to speak to Pharaoh for the first time
Moses and Aaron convey the same message 'Let my people go, so that they may hold a feast for me' to Pharaoh
The same command 'Let my people go, so that they may serve me' is repeated at the first plague
Repeated command to Pharaoh to let the people go so that they may serve the Lord
Moses is told to rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh with the same message
The same formulation 'the Lord, the God of the Hebrews' and the command to let the people go
The same question from 'the Lord, the God of the Hebrews' to Pharaoh to let the people go
The command to fear the Lord and serve him alone is linked to the people's calling to serve God
Stephen quotes God's words to Moses about delivering the people from Egypt
Repeated prophetic demand just before the following plagues, emphasizing God's unshakable will for freedom for service.
Earlier repetition of the same demand before the third plague, showing the progression in the confrontation.
Contrast between Pharaoh's compromising offer and God's absolute demand for full freedom.
Theological explanation of why the demand for liberation meets resistance: God hardening Pharaoh's heart.
